findings.title: Document title is missing or empty
findings.summary: The page has no usable <title>. Search results show a generated name instead of the intended one, which costs clicks. Observed: document.title is empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a unique 30 to 60 character title that names the page and the brand.

findings.title: Meta description is missing
findings.summary: Without a meta description, search engines assemble the snippet themselves, which usually reads worse than a written one. Observed: meta[name=description] is missing or empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 120 to 160 character meta description that states the page offer.

findings.title: Page has no h1 heading

findings.suggested_fix: Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio reaches 4.5:1.

findings.title: Page language is not declared
findings.summary: The html element has no lang attribute, so screen readers may read the page with the wrong pronunciation rules. Reported on 1 element(s).
findings.suggested_fix: Set lang on the html element, for example <html lang="en">.

findings.title: Image has no text alternative
findings.summary: An image carries no alt attribute, so its content is lost for screen reader users and for search engines. Reported on 1 element(s).
findings.suggested_fix: Add alt text describing the content, or an empty alt if it is decorative.

findings.title: Form field has no accessible name
findings.summary: A field in the page form has no label, aria-label or title. A screen reader announces nothing, so the primary action cannot be completed without sight. Reported on 1 element(s).
findings.suggested_fix: Associate a visible <label for> with the field, or add aria-label.

findings.title: Link has no accessible name
findings.summary: A link contains no text and no aria-label. Screen reader users hear the raw URL or nothing at all, and cannot tell where the link leads. Reported on 2 element(s).
findings.suggested_fix: Add link text or aria-label; for icon links describe the destination.

findings.title: Header site-name link is only 19 CSS pixels tall (header > a:nth-of-type(1))
findings.summary: The header link html:nth-of-type(1) > body:nth-of-type(1) > header:nth-of-type(1) > a:nth-of-type(1) measures 94.421875 by 19 CSS pixels on 390x844, so it is shorter than the WCAG 2.5.8 target-size minimum and a touch user aiming at the site name can miss it.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the header link block padding or a min-height so its pointer target reaches 24 by 24 CSS pixels without changing the visual text size.

root_causes.label: header
root_causes.summary: Header navigation links have no accessible names and are covered by other elements, so visitors cannot tell where links lead or click them reliably.
root_causes.rationale: Fixing the header closes several symptoms at once: the links gain names a screen reader can announce, and a pointer user can activate the covered link where it appears. Left alone, someone tabbing or tapping through the header meets links that announce nothing or do not respond.
